methodologyNotes: Specs sourced from manufacturer product pages (radpowerbikes.com, aventon.com, lectricebikes.com, ride1up.com) and reputable review aggregators (electricbikereview.com). Manufacturer pages for Specialized and Trek blocked 403/404 for direct scraping; electricbikereview.com served as primary source for those brands. priceUsd = US MSRP or starting price for the base/reference config (note: sale prices excluded where MSRP is documented). motor_w = nominal/rated wattage (not peak). range_mi = manufacturer claimed max or real-world tested depending on source; see provenance. weight_lb = total weight with battery unless noted. class = US e-bike class (1/2/3). throttle = true if any throttle mode available. release = model year or year launched. RadCity 5 Plus was discontinued ca. 2022; replaced in lineup by Radster Road (2024). Trek FX+ 2 was discontinued; current FX+ lineup is the FX+ 1S (2025). Soltera 2.5 is the current Soltera model (2024). Aventure.3 HS is the current Aventure (2025). A null beats any guess. All sources accessed 2026-06-15.

products.name: Rad Power Bikes Radster Road
products.provenance: radpowerbikes.com product page: 750W motor, 28 mph, 720Wh battery, Class 1-3 switchable (ships Class 3), 74.5 lbs, half-twist throttle, $1,999. Range 25-65 miles manufacturer estimate. electricbikereview.com confirms: real-world 53.3 miles tested, same specs and $1,999 price. This is the successor to the discontinued RadCity 5 Plus in the commuter segment.

products.name: Rad Power Bikes RadRunner Plus
products.provenance: radpowerbikes.com product page: 750W, 20 mph, 624Wh, Class 2, 75 lbs, throttle yes, $1,799. electricbikereview.com confirms 750W, 20 mph, 672Wh (earlier model had 672Wh; 2025 update shows 624Wh per manufacturer page), 74.4 lbs, $1,899 (older MSRP). Range 25-55 miles manufacturer estimate; 45 mi midpoint used. Utility/cargo commuter segment.

products.name: Rad Power Bikes RadRunner Max
products.priceNote: US MSRP base single-battery config, radpowerbikes.com 2025
products.provenance: radpowerbikes.com product page: 750W, 28 mph, 672Wh, Class 1-3 switchable, 82 lbs (with battery), throttle (half-twist grip), $2,299. Range 60+ miles single battery per manufacturer. electricbikereview.com confirms all specs and $2,299 MSRP, 2025 model year.

products.name: Aventon Level.3
products.provenance: electricbikereview.com (two separate accesses confirm): 500W rear hub, 28 mph, 708Wh (36V 20Ah), Class 3, 67 lbs, no throttle (pedal assist only), $1,899 MSRP, 2025 model. Manufacturer claimed range 70 miles; review tested 75 miles at minimum assist. Range_mi set to 70 (manufacturer claim). Corroboration URL same source — manufacturer aventon.com page returned 404 during scrape.

products.name: Aventon Aventure.3 HS
products.priceNote: US MSRP (sale price was $1,799 at time of access; $1,999 is stated MSRP), aventon.com 2025
products.provenance: electricbikereview.com (aventure-3 and aventure-3-hs pages): 750W nominal (1188W peak), 28 mph, 733Wh, Class 2 (adjustable to Class 3 via app), 76 lbs, throttle yes, MSRP $1,999 (sale $1,799 observed). Range 62 miles Eco mode, 34 miles Turbo mode per manufacturer; 62 used. Fat-tire off-road commuter segment. 2025 model year.

products.name: Aventon Soltera 2.5
products.provenance: electricbikereview.com (soltera-2-5 page): 350W rear hub, 20 mph, 345.6Wh (rounded to 346), Class 2, 46 lbs, throttle yes (both PAS and throttle capped at 20 mph Class 2), $1,199 MSRP, 2024 model. Real-world range 27-48 miles; manufacturer claims 46 miles — 46 used. Lightweight city e-bike segment. Note: earlier Soltera 2 review shows 'No throttle' which may refer to the step-over variant; 2.5 confirmed has throttle.

products.name: Lectric XP4 (500W)
products.provenance: electricbikereview.com (xp4-review): 500W nominal (1092W peak), 28 mph (toggleable Class 2/3), 499Wh (48V 10.4Ah), Class 2 as shipped, 70.7 lbs with battery (rounded to 71), thumb throttle, $999. Manufacturer claims 50 miles; real-world 44 miles tested. lectricebikes.com confirms $999 base price and 500W/28 mph. Folding fat-tire commuter. 2025 model year.

products.name: Lectric XP4 750W
products.provenance: electricbikereview.com (xp4-750-review page): 750W nominal (1310W peak), 28 mph, 840Wh (48V 17.5Ah), Class 2/3 switchable, thumb throttle, $1,299. Weight: source lists 61 lbs WITHOUT battery; with the 7.1 lb battery the total is ~68.1 lbs. weight_lb corrected to 68 (total-with-battery) for consistency with dataset methodology. Manufacturer claims 85 miles range; used as stated. lectricebikes.com confirms $1,299 price and 750W variant.

products.name: Lectric XPedition 2.0
products.priceNote: US MSRP base single-battery config, lectricebikes.com 2024
products.provenance: electricbikereview.com (lectric-xpedition-2-review): 750W nominal (1310W peak), 28 mph, Class 3, 624Wh base battery (dual-battery 1248Wh and long-range 1680Wh also available), 74 lbs, $1,399 base. throttle corrected false->true: the XPedition 2.0 ships with a thumb throttle (a headline upgrade over the v1 twist throttle) in addition to its torque-sensor PAS 1-5; confirmed by lectricebikes.com xpedition-series page (Thumb Throttle) and multiple reviews. Range 60-170 miles depending on battery config; 60 miles used for base single-battery. Cargo/family e-bike segment, 450 lb payload capacity. lectricebikes.com confirms lineup and pricing.

products.name: Specialized Turbo Vado SL 2 6.0
products.priceNote: US MSRP EQ (equipped) model, electricbikereview.com 2024; 5.0 base starts ~$5,500
products.provenance: electricbikereview.com (turbo-vado-sl page, Vado SL 2 6.0 review): Specialized SL 1.2 mid-drive motor 320W (50 Nm), 28 mph Class 3, 520Wh internal (680Wh with optional 160Wh range extender), 39 lbs, no throttle (pedal assist only), $6,500 for EQ tested model. Range: tested over 100 miles in Eco mode (manufacturer claims 103 miles). Lightest e-bike in this dataset. Carbon frame. Two review pages confirm same core specs.

products.name: Trek FX+ 1S
products.priceNote: US MSRP, trekbikes.com 2025 (electricbikereview.com cites $1,999; Trek website shows $2,199.99)
products.provenance: electricbikereview.com (trek/fx-plus-1s): 500W motor, 28 mph, 520Wh, Class 3, 48.3 lbs (rounded to 48), throttle yes, $1,999 per review. trekbikes.com catalog page shows FX+ 1S at $2,199.99 (current pricing). Trek FX+ 2 was discontinued; FX+ 1S is the current entry-level FX+ in the fitness commuter segment. Range 52 miles tested at minimum assist.
